climate_pressure: Pasture degradation and climatic stress in the dzud-resilience assessment.
documented_impact: Herders seek Otor pasture in other aimags as grazing access becomes constrained.
fcv_mediator: Unequal access and limited systematic management of movement and shared pasture can mediate resource competition.
possible_consequence: The report describes disputes between incoming herders and local users, without event counts or armed-conflict evidence.
alternative_explanations: Herd size, grazing pressure and land-management arrangements also affect degradation and disputes.
Not all mobility or resource competition produces conflict.
uncertainty: Qualitative source-stated mechanism, not a measured climate-attributable conflict effect or a prediction for named receiving settlements. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: Transparent shared-pasture rules and monitoring are proposed governance responses, not evaluated conflict-reduction interventions.
compact_statement: Pasture stress and inter-aimag grazing mobility can interact with access and governance constraints to produce disputes; armed conflict is not established.
